newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia lowers JV oil output duties, hits exporters.
newsitem.headline: Russia lowers JV oil output duties, hits exporters.

text.p: A Russian government decree has set a new 30,000 rouble-per-tonne tariff for oil exporters who are not producers, and set a new, lower range of duties on domestically-produced oil, the government said on Friday.
The government press service, in a copy of the decree, also said certain joint ventures would pay a privileged, 20,000 rouble tariff for each tonne of produced oil.

The new rate was long sought by qualified joint ventures with priority access rights to Russia's crowded pipeline system. The old rate was just over 56,000 roubles. Qualified joint ventures are those with export tariff exemptions.
All of the new tariffs are retroactive to November 1, 1996.

The decree named the ventures paying the new 20,000 rouble rate as KomiArcticOil (with British Gas Plc ), AmKomi (with Aminex Plc of Britain), White Nights (with Phibro Energy Inc and Anglo-Suisse), Severnaya Neft, the Siberian-American Oil Company (SANK) (with Pennzoil Co), Chernogorskoye (with Anderman Smith of the United States), Petrosakh (with U.S. Petroleum), Polar Lights (Conoco Inc, a subsidiary of Dupont Co.) and Ritek.
Ritek has only Russian, not foreign, participants, a Ritek spokesman said. The Petroleum Advisory Forum had no information on Severnaya Neft.
Other joint ventures will pay higher output duties, while Russian oil companies will pay duties in the new range of 700 roubles to 95,460 roubles per tonne of produced oil.
The tariffs do not include Russian value-added tax, whose basic rate is 20 percent.
The new production-tariff range lowers the average duty to 55,000 roubles from 72,000 roubles, a government spokesman familiar with the decree said.

The decree said non-producing exporters buying crude oil at Russia's below-world prices must pay the 30,000 rouble tariff in addition to the production excise duty owed by the Russian company that produced the oil.
The decree will be formally enacted by February 15, the date by which tax and customs authorities must sign documents that put it into force.
All of the tariffs cover gas condensate output and exports.
The decree said the Nobel Oil joint venture, with Glencore AG of Switzerland, was the only venture fully exempt from paying a production tariff.
Seven Russian companies, including AO Sakhalinmorneftegaz and YUNKO (the Chechen Oil Company) are also exempt.
